violated_invariant: Collateral valuation must not be movable within a transaction by an unprivileged donation; the oracle for wrapped xStock collateral tracked an ERC4626 convertToAssets() rate that a direct underlying transfer inflates.
notes: AaveOracle (0xbd49) is unmodified Aave v3 code; getAssetPrice simply returns latestAnswer() from the configured per-asset source. The actual manipulable logic sits in the wGOOGLx price adapter / ERC4626 wrapper (0x1630, unverified, not a candidate), so the defect in recovered source is the trust placed in that source. None of the Slither findings describe a manipulable price source; calls-loop and missing-zero-check are true but harmless.

violated_invariant: Vault share price must not be inflatable by a same-transaction donation; FleetCommander NAV is the live, unguarded sum of each Ark's totalAssets(), including an Ark being offboarded whose Silo vgUSDC position was counted at par.
notes: FleetCommander deployed at block 21795049, before the fork, so the recovered source is pre-patch. NAV is computed by looping _arks[i].totalAssets() with no donation or deviation guard (the NatSpec itself says it relies on accurate Ark reporting); public analyses add that the donated-into Ark had been capped to zero for offboarding but was still in the active set. The calls-loop findings on _sumTotalAssets touch the defect line but describe gas/DoS risk, not the inflatable valuation, so they do not explain the exploit.

violated_invariant: A single actor should not be able to buy a quorum of votes on the open market, pass a proposal that hands over the ProxyAdmin, and upgrade a fund-holding proxy; a 200k-vote quorum against instantly-minable STRNGR votes made this cheap.
notes: The catalog victims are both AdminUpgradeabilityProxy forwarders; the Governor implementation (0xf6c7...) and StrongPoolV5 implementation (0xe89c...) that hold the quorum and mineForVotesOnly logic were not recovered, so no defect location can be named from source. Kept in scope as governance_design rather than designed behavior because the taxonomy explicitly covers governance capture, but the contracts did execute their rules as written. The incorrect-return / incorrect-modifier findings on the proxies are the usual false positives on the ifAdmin fallback pattern.

violated_invariant: The factory must only ever issue the intended initializePool/mint calls to the PositionManager on behalf of itself; forwarding caller-supplied bytes verbatim let anyone make the factory call setApprovalForAll on every LP NFT it custodies.
notes: launch() is permissionless and passes initCalldata and modifyCalldata straight into IPositionManager.multicall with no selector or target validation, which is exactly the forwarded call the PoC abuses. Slither has no finding for this: arbitrary-send-eth (index 0) is about the dust refund to msg.sender, which is intended, so it is marked invalid; the unchecked-transfer and unused-return hits on launch are real but cosmetic.

violated_invariant: Redeeming X FUM in one defund() should pay at least as much ETH as redeeming X FUM across many consecutive defund() calls; the averaged sliding-price approximation plus per-call adjShrinkFactor contraction is not split-invariant.
notes: ethFromDefund prices a burn off the arithmetic mean of the starting and an estimated ending FUM sell price, and each call shrinks bidAskAdjustment, so slicing one redemption into 64 pieces pays more ETH than the lump sum; no oracle input moves. The divide-before-multiply findings sit in checkForFreshOraclePrice and _storeState, not in the redemption curve, and do not describe the flaw. The reentrancy-no-eth on _defundFum is marked invalid because the only pre-state-write external call is to the protocol's own FUM token.

violated_invariant: Share mint/burn valuation must not depend on the instantaneous Uniswap V3 slot0 price; the vault's TWAP/deviation guard covered only the manager rebalance path, so a swap-skewed tick let a caller mint and burn at a favourable token mix.
notes: The only victim candidate is the EIP173Proxy; the ArrakisVaultV1 implementation (0xd68b...) that holds mint/burn/getUnderlyingBalances was not recovered, so the location names come from the PoC and public G-UNI source, not from a recovered candidate. The proxy's controlled-delegatecall finding is the owner-gated init-call pattern and is not the exploited weakness.

violated_invariant: Voting power over a vault should track a meaningful share of the vault's economic ownership; because only ~0.05 gtmvETH of wrapped shares existed, one depositor who wrapped a single share held a supermajority and could pass a proposal that rerouted the vault's debt to an attacker strategy.
notes: None of the six candidates (Yearn V3 meta-vault, Aragon TokenVoting, DAO, Zodiac modifiers, wrapped governance token) has recovered source, so no code location or Slither adjudication is possible. The PoC reconstructs a legitimate proposal/vote/execute flow rather than a key compromise, so it is kept in scope under governance_design with the same designed-behavior caveat as StrongBlock.

violated_invariant: Only the current manager may change the delegate implementations that item-adapter clones delegatecall into; an unprotected, re-runnable initialize() let any caller become manager and register code that transfers items without owner approval.
notes: The catalog carries no victim address; the two contract registries hijacked via initialize()/acceptManager() and the ERC-1155 platform are unverified, so the only recovered candidate is the ENJToken, which is merely the drained asset. Root cause follows the PoC's trace description of a re-runnable initializer that reassigns the manager; it could not be checked against source.

violated_invariant: A liquidation must not let a party controlling both the borrower and the taker extract more collateral value than the quote it repays; Ajna's oracle-free auction/bucket pricing and the bucketTake/take/repayDebt accounting let the attacker's self-liquidation shift the loss onto other lenders.
notes: The pool proxy 0xad24 is unverified and the ERC20Pool implementation (0x05bb...) is not a candidate, so no Slither findings exist on the victim; the only sourced candidate is the cbETH FiatTokenProxy, which is the collateral token. Press coverage agrees it was internal liquidation accounting rather than an oracle attack but no technical post-mortem names the exact flawed computation, hence low confidence on the precise mechanism.

violated_invariant: Pool shares minted by a single-asset join must be backed by a proportional token input; with the 8-decimal WBTC reserve compressed to dust, calcSingleInGivenPoolOut rounds the required input down to one satoshi while the full BPT is still minted, and joinswapPoolAmountOut has no minimum-effective-input or precision check.
notes: joinswapPoolAmountOut only requires tokenAmountIn != 0, <= maxAmountIn and <= MAX_IN_RATIO of the balance, so a 1-satoshi input for a large poolAmountOut passes once the reserve is dust; MIN_BALANCE is enforced only in bind/rebind. Slither raises nothing on this path; the reentrancy findings on joinPool/exitPool are marked invalid because both run under the _lock_ mutex.
